en: Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: There was a king among those who came before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old, so send me a boy whom I may teach sorcery.' So he sent him a boy to teach him. Along the boy’s path when he traveled was a monk, so he sat with him and listened to his speech, and it pleased him. Whenever he went to the sorcerer, he would pass by the monk and sit with him, and when he arrived at the sorcerer's, the sorcerer would beat him. The boy complained of that to the monk, so the monk said: 'When you fear the sorcerer, say: My family detained me; and when you fear your family, say: The sorcerer detained me.' While he was in that state, he came upon an enormous beast that had blocked the people from passing. The boy said: 'Today I will know whether the sorcerer is superior or the monk is superior.' He took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if the affair of the monk is more beloved to You than the affair of the sorcerer, then kill this beast so that the people may pass.' He threw it at the beast and killed it, and the people passed. He then came to the monk and informed him, and the monk said to him: 'O my little son, today you are superior to me; your affair has reached what I see. You will surely be tested, so if you are tested, do not point to me.' The boy used to heal the blind from birth and the leper, and he treated people for all kinds of illnesses. A courtier of the king who had become blind heard of him, so he came to him with many gifts and said: 'All that is here is yours if you heal me.' He said: 'I do not heal anyone; it is only Allah Who heals. If you believe in Allah, I will supplicate Allah, and He will heal you.' So he believed in Allah, and Allah healed him. He then went to the king and sat beside him as he used to sit. The king said to him: 'Who restored your sight to you?' He said: 'My Lord.' The king said: 'Do you have a lord other than me?' He said: 'My Lord and your Lord is Allah.' So the king seized him and kept torturing him until he pointed to the boy. The boy was brought, and the king said to him: 'O my son, your sorcery has reached the point where you heal the blind from birth and the leper, and you do such and such!' He said: 'I do not heal anyone; it is only Allah Who heals.' So he seized him and kept torturing him until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and it was said to him: 'Recant your religion!' But he refused. The king then called for a saw, placed the saw in the parting of his head, and sawed him in half until his two halves fell apart. Then the courtier of the king was brought, and it was said to him: 'Recant your religion!' But he refused. So he placed the saw in the parting of his head and sawed him in half until his two halves fell apart. Then the boy was brought, and it was said to him: 'Recant your religion!' But he refused. The king handed him over to a group of his companions and said: 'Take him to such-and-such mountain, ascend the mountain with him, and when you reach its peak, if he recants his religion, well and good; otherwise, hurl him down.' They took him and climbed the mountain with him, and the boy said: 'O Allah, save me from them by whatever means You will.' The mountain shook beneath them and they fell off, and the boy came walking back to the king. The king said to him: 'What happened to your companions?' He said: 'Allah saved me from them.' The king then handed him over to a group of his companions and said: 'Take him, carry him in a small boat, and go to the middle of the sea. If he recants his religion, well and good; otherwise, cast him into the sea.' They took him, and he said: 'O Allah, save me from them by whatever means You will.' The boat capsized with them and they drowned, and the boy came walking back to the king. The king said to him: 'What happened to your companions?' He said: 'Allah saved me from them.' Then the boy said to the king: 'You will not be able to kill me until you do what I command you to do.' The king said: 'And what is that?' He said: 'You must gather the people in a single open plain, crucify me upon the trunk of a tree, take an arrow from my quiver, place the arrow in the notch of the bow, and then say: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy. Then shoot me. For indeed, if you do that, you will kill me.' So the king gathered the people in a single open plain, crucified him upon a tree trunk, took an arrow from his quiver, placed the arrow in the notch of the bow, and said: 'In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.' He then shot him, and the arrow struck his temple. The boy placed his hand on his temple at the site of the arrow, and died. Thereupon the people said: 'We believe in the Lord of the boy! We believe in the Lord of the boy! We believe in the Lord of the boy!' The king was approached, and it was said to him: 'Do you see what you were fearing? By Allah, that which you feared has indeed befallen you; the people have believed!' So he ordered that trenches be dug at the openings of the roads, and they were dug, and he ignited fires in them. He said: 'Whoever does not recant his religion, plunge him into it,' or it was said to them: 'Leap into it!' They did so until a woman came with a young child of hers, and she hesitated to plunge into it. Her infant boy said to her: 'O my mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth!'
